text:
alex: Heads up — two customers reported duplicate billing today after a series of 429s and client retries. Looks like a burst-credit race when idempotency is missing. Anyone seen this pattern before? :ambulance:

maria: Ugh. Do we have traces/request IDs to prove it was retries vs legit double submits?

alex: Yep. trace ids: r_1a2b3c and r_1a2b3d — same payload, no Idempotency-Key header on the subsequent requests. Billing service increments usage on receipt, then downstream commit occasionally races with retry that also increments.

sam: That matches a race I hit last quarter — we were doing `increment -> commit` in two RPCs so retries could double-increment if the original commit didn't ack before client retry.

nora: Is this per-key or per-org? Are burst credits in play?

alex: Per-org counters are fine. Problem happens when per-key (API key) quota + burst credits get consumed and the request path does a non-atomic reserve then finalize. If client retries before ack, second attempt gets through and we charge twice.

paul: We should add a safe-guard at the gateway: require/validate Idempotency-Key for any billing-impacting POSTs OR do an automatic dedup by body hash. But body-hash has issues with streaming/attachments.

maria: Short-term mitigation: reject retries without Idempotency-Key with a 400, or return a special 429-with-retry-after that suggests adding idempotency. Long-term: atomic reserve+commit.

sam: Implementation idea: use a single atomic Lua script in Redis for `check+reserve` that returns a tombstone if already reserved. Pseudocode:
```lua
-- KEYS[1] = idempotency_key
-- ARGV[1] = tokens
local val = redis.call('GET', KEYS[1])
if val then
  return {"already", val}
end
redis.call('SET', KEYS[1], ARGV[1], 'EX', 60) -- short TTL for reservation
-- also atomically decrement org bucket here or fail and cleanup
return {"reserved"}
```
This prevents two concurrent requests from both reserving.

nora: We also need a billing checkpoint pattern: do not apply final invoice/charge until `commit` which validates reservation idempotency record. That prevents double finalization if increments were accidentally applied.

alex: Agree. Also want telemetry: a `duplicate_charge_detected` event and a dashboard panel in Console showing "dedup window conflicts" per org/key with sample traces. Paul, can you add an alert when per-key duplicate count > 0.1% of requests in 5m?

paul: Yep, I'll add a per-key metric and a rate rule. Also recommend adding a traceback sample in the alert payload so SRE can triage quickly.

maria: Rollout plan: 1) Quick: enforce Idempotency-Key for POST /v1/generate for paid plans behind a feature flag, return 400 if missing. 2) Mid: gateway auto-reserve with body-hash for non-streaming routes. 3) Long: atomic Redis reservation + commit and billing checkpoint refactor + telemetry + console panel. Canary on 5% orgs then 25%.

sam: For the Lua route, I'll write the script + unit tests. We'll need to ensure the reservation step also accounts for burst credits (i.e., decrement burst counter inside the same atomic op).

nora: Also need a recovery process for duplicates already charged — a backfill to detect customers that got double-charged and issue credits. We should surface that in CS playbook.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-214 (link) — labeled billing/dup-charge, severity P2. Assigned: unassigned.

alex: Thanks — can sam + nora pick up the ticket? Sam for gateway/Lua, Nora for billing checkpoint + CS runbook. I'll own the Console panel and alert work with Paul.

paul: I'll stub the dashboard tiles and add metrics to telemetry pipeline.

maria: One more note — streaming endpoints can't rely on body-hash. For them we should require explicit Idempotency-Key. Add docs/SDK guidance to auto-set a UUID idempotency on client retry logic. :lock:

alex: Great. Let's sync briefly in 30m to confirm ownership and timelines. :thumbsup:
